title: Left Join Records
summary: Implement a SQL-style LEFT JOIN over two lists of dicts, with one-to-many matches and column clashes.

stages.title: LEFT JOIN
stages.requirement:
Write `left_join(left, right, on)` with SQL `LEFT JOIN` semantics over lists of dicts:

- Every left row appears in the output at least once, **in left order**.
- For each left row, emit one output row per matching right row (`right[on] == left[on]`),
  with matches in **right order** (one-to-many).
- A left row with no match is emitted once, with every right-only column set to `None`.
  The right-only columns are the union of keys across **all** right rows, minus `on`.
- Column clash: if a non-`on` column exists in both rows, the left value is kept under its
  name, and the right value goes to `"<column>_right"`.
- Rows whose `on` value is `None` never match (like SQL `NULL`).
- Don't mutate the inputs.

```python
users = [{"id": 1, "name": "ada"}, {"id": 2, "name": "bob"}]
orders = [{"id": 1, "total": 10}, {"id": 1, "total": 5}]
left_join(users, orders, "id")
# -> [{"id": 1, "name": "ada", "total": 10},
#     {"id": 1, "name": "ada", "total": 5},
#     {"id": 2, "name": "bob", "total": None}]
```

Up to 50,000 rows on each side, so avoid nested loops.

visibleTests.name: test_example
visibleTests.code:
def test_example():
    users = [{"id": 1, "name": "ada"}, {"id": 2, "name": "bob"}]
    orders = [{"id": 1, "total": 10}, {"id": 1, "total": 5}]
    assert left_join(users, orders, "id") == [
        {"id": 1, "name": "ada", "total": 10},
        {"id": 1, "name": "ada", "total": 5},
        {"id": 2, "name": "bob", "total": None},
    ]

hiddenTests.name: test_column_clash
hiddenTests.code:
def test_column_clash():
    left = [{"k": 1, "status": "active"}]
    right = [{"k": 1, "status": "shipped"}]
    assert left_join(left, right, "k") == [{"k": 1, "status": "active", "status_right": "shipped"}]

hiddenTests.name: test_unmatched_gets_union_of_right_columns
hiddenTests.description: Matched rows only carry their own columns; unmatched rows get None for every right column.
hiddenTests.code:
def test_unmatched_gets_union_of_right_columns():
    left = [{"k": 1}, {"k": 9}]
    right = [{"k": 1, "a": "x"}, {"k": 2, "b": "y"}]
    assert left_join(left, right, "k") == [
        {"k": 1, "a": "x"},
        {"k": 9, "a": None, "b": None},
    ]

def test_none_keys_never_match():
    left = [{"k": None, "v": 1}]
    right = [{"k": None, "w": 2}]
    assert left_join(left, right, "k") == [{"k": None, "v": 1, "w": None}]

def test_inputs_not_mutated():
    left = [{"k": 1}]
    right = [{"k": 1, "x": 2}]
    left_join(left, right, "k")
    assert left == [{"k": 1}] and right == [{"k": 1, "x": 2}]

hints: This is a hash join: index the right side by the join key once, then probe it for each left row.
Build `dict[key, list[row]]` for the right side, skipping `None` keys. Collect the union of right columns while you're at it.
For each output row, start from a copy of the left row, then add right columns, renaming clashes to `<col>_right`.

solution.explanation:
A hash join: one pass over the right side builds `key -> [rows]` (skipping `None`, which
never matches) and collects the union of right columns. Each left row then probes the
index. Matched rows merge each right row in right order. Unmatched rows merge a
synthetic all-`None` row, so they get every right column. Merging into a fresh `dict`
leaves the inputs untouched.
